reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a leveraged flash-loan arbitrage setup and presents automated trading as rapidly increasing about $230 to $1,200. It links participation to funding a contract with KCS and paying approximately 40 KCS in gas to earn more than the demonstrated amount, while urging viewers to act before the opportunity stops working.

citations.quote: KCS KuCoin Flash loan Arbitrage Trading Bot | 10x Leverage Trading with KCS !
setup an arbitrage attack on two DEXs on KCC Mainnet; You will create the coin on MojitoSwap and then trade this coin rapidly against KoffeeSwap
you need to be at get your metam to get to the starting point and get your MetaMask hooked to the kcc chain
I'm a fund this with about $200 worth and that's enough to cover the gas for a loan amount of 600 KCS
once I confirm this goes through, we're going to run the flash loan and then we're going to sit back and wait for the profits to hit

opening.argument: Judge the profit claim in the context of the speaker's own qualification: "It won't work forever the DEXs will catch on." The speaker presents the result as time-sensitive, not as a return that will persist. The description also identifies a substantial required cost, "APPROX 40 KCS," rather than concealing what participation would require. Those qualifications do not prove the trade is sound, but they leave a narrower claim than a guaranteed-return pitch: a claimed result under conditions the speaker says may change.

citations.quote: It won't work forever the DEXs will catch on.
NEW GAS FEE REQUIRED: APPROX 40 KCS

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that the speaker expects profits after funding the contract. But "we're going to sit back and wait for the profits to hit" describes what the speaker expects in this run; it does not establish a promise that every viewer will receive the same return. Its opening also omits the speaker's warning that the opportunity may stop working. The demonstrated increase warrants scrutiny, but the cited language does not, by itself, establish a guaranteed payout.

citations.quote: once I confirm this goes through, we're going to run the flash loan and then we're going to sit back and wait for the profits to hit
It won't work forever the DEXs will catch on.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A warning that the method may stop working does not neutralize the solicitation. The speaker says viewers should take advantage before it stops, while reporting that about $230 became $1,200 through automated trading. The description explicitly tells viewers to increase the gas fee to earn more than the video shows. These are inducements tied to funding a contract and expecting returns, even without an explicit promise that returns are guaranteed.

citations.quote: I think everyone should take advantage while the offering gets into those because it won't last forever.
I just went about $230 to $1,200 using code to automate trading
TO EARN MORE THAN THE AMOUNT IN THE VIDEO YOU CAN INCREASE GAS FEE

opening.argument: The video spends its instructional sequence on setting up a development environment: connecting MetaMask to KCC, bringing source code into a fresh Remix workspace, compiling it, and connecting Remix to the wallet. The speaker then walks through deploying a contract with a token name, symbol and loan amount. That is a concrete software demonstration, not merely an unsupported profit slogan. The later claimed result is presented as the outcome of the speaker's run; it does not establish that a viewer has obtained the same result.

You are starting in a fresh workspace and the source code can be found in the video description.
we need to set our remit's compile to 0.50, and everything should compile.
we have to come up with a token name symbol and loan amount

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution cites wallet setup and contract funding, but those steps also have an ordinary reading within the demonstrated deployment workflow. The speaker says the contract is funded to cover gas for a stated loan amount, then shows the steps that follow. The title's trading-bot language describes the subject of the tutorial; it does not independently verify that the code works or show that the speaker receives viewers' funds.

citations.quote: I'm a fund this with about $200 worth and that's enough to cover the gas for a loan amount of 600 KCS
KCS KuCoin Flash loan Arbitrage Trading Bot | 10x Leverage Trading with KCS !

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The technical walkthrough is part of the inducement, not a substitute for it. The speaker directs the viewer toward source code and wallet setup, then says funding the contract precedes waiting for profits. The description expressly connects a higher gas fee with earning more, and the speaker reports a rapid monetary increase. A demonstration can still promote the funded-contract returns it purports to demonstrate.

I just went about $230 to $1,200 using code to automate trading

opening.argument: The description names external tools and exchanges, including MetaMask, Remix, MojitoSwap and KoffeeSwap, while the speaker describes creating a token and trading it across exchanges. The funding instruction is expressly framed as sending KCS to the contract the speaker has just deployed. These sources do not identify a recipient controlled by the speaker, ask viewers for credentials, or describe a referral or downline payment. That absence does not certify the code as safe, but it matters when distinguishing a risky trading tutorial from a demonstrated scheme to collect viewers' assets.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution establishes that money is put into a contract and that the speaker expects profit. It does not establish from its cited excerpts who controls the deployed contract or where its funds ultimately go. Even the speaker's stated reason for funding is to cover gas for the claimed loan amount. The profit claim may be unreliable, but unreliability alone does not fill those evidentiary gaps.

citations.quote: I'm a fund this with about $200 worth and that's enough to cover the gas for a loan amount of 600 KCS

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A credential request or proven diversion of funds is not necessary to recognize what this video promotes. The speaker instructs viewers through a funded-contract workflow, says to wait for profits, and reports turning about $230 into $1,200. The description goes further by telling viewers they can increase the gas fee to earn more. Missing proof of the contract's ultimate recipient does not erase the direct appeal to fund it in pursuit of returns.
